title: Cap and sort four pens
instruction: Fit each pen with a cap of the same color. Put the two red pens on the left and the two blue pens on the right.
context: Preparing pens for storage requires fitting the right closures, keeping the caps attached and sorting the finished pens by color.
setup: Physical reproduction specifies pigmented polypropylene pen bodies and cap shells, polyester felt nibs and printed paper destination markers. These are chosen materials, not measured catalog composition; physical cap retention remains unresolved. Simulation uses rigid bodies and color shaders. The YAM station uses x forward, y left and z up; coordinates are in metres and the tabletop is at z=0.7475. There are four pens, each 165.2 mm long with a 19.4 mm barrel and a mass of 35 g, plus four separate hollow caps, each 35 mm long, about 32.6 mm across and 8 g. Pen starting roots (x, y, yaw in degrees) are red (0.16, -0.16, -100), blue (0.29, -0.15, -80), red (0.42, -0.16, -65) and blue (0.21, -0.34, -110), all at z=0.7575. Corresponding cap roots are red (0.18, 0.15, -120), blue (0.38, 0.32, -105), red (0.40, 0.10, -145) and blue (0.24, 0.05, -125), all at z=0.7638. Objects settle from these poses. Flat 240 × 200 mm destination prints sit 0.3 mm above the table: red on the left at (0.300, 0.230), blue on the right at (0.300, -0.230). Seed 0, no jitter. Cameras record at 640 × 360, with the original station top-camera pose and intrinsics and unchanged wrist calibrations.
scoring: Score the final state. Each pen earns 0.125 for a matching cap retained after measured insertion and one second with both hands clear, plus 0.125 for resting in its correct area for one second. Capping credit lasts while the matching pair remains retained; placement credit is lost if the pen is held or moved out. Wrong-color and uncapped pens earn no placement credit. Rest requires the pen root 6–25 mm above the table, its axis within 8° of horizontal and norm(linear velocity) + 0.06 × norm(angular velocity) < 0.015 m/s. The conservative projected pen/cap envelope must fit inside the rectangle with a 1 mm inset. Both tool-center points must be more than 60 mm from the full pen segment and cap. Full score requires all four matching caps retained and all four pens released and resting in the correct areas.
reset_notes: Remove all cap-retention joints, restore the separate pens and caps to their starting poses, clear insertion, release and scoring histories, and capture fresh observations after clearing camera history.
fidelity: Catalog barrel visuals use analytic rigid pen collisions. PP shells and polyester nibs are reproduction specifications, not simulated material compliance. A 25 mm cap bore leaves 2.8 mm radial clearance around the 19.4 mm barrel; no physical retention feature exists. Aligned insertion and 0.2 s seating trigger a pose-preserving fixed joint with no calibrated pull-off force. Caps stay joined until reset or seating invalidation. Prints are flat. Physical retention needs geometry/physics revision.
